verdict.rationale: Rollbar documents its own project and account access tokens with scopes. A client-side token is limited to the post_client_item scope and "can't be used to read any data", and tokens can be disabled and replaced at any time, so least-privilege credentials exist natively. Evidence on the full scope set is thin, and nothing ties scoped tokens to agent use such as the MCP server. Missing for 10: documented full scope catalog (read/write/server scopes), agent- or MCP-specific credential guidance, token expiry/TTL controls, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Use a separate client-side token with post_client_item scope only.
The client-side access token can only be used to send events and only from client-side platforms. It can't be used to read any data
Tokens can be disabled and replaced at any time.
